capabilities.local_comparison: Compare two local controller solves at the same saved state/previous input/horizon with exactly one adopted weight change. Measures local plan/endpoint differences; does not establish closed-loop settling or causal attribution. Requires a saved effective horizon matching the authorized horizon.
capabilities.prediction_braking: At one saved projected state, compare recorded input with instantaneous braking-box input over the fixed short horizon. Can measure local endpoint speed/position differences. Cannot separate objective weighting, seed selection, horizon effects or backend-model mismatch when they predict the same result; cannot identify the dominant settling cause.

discriminating_observations: Sign and magnitude of (recorded-input endpoint speed - braking-box endpoint speed) at this single saved state.
Whether the braking-box endpoint speed falls below the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit over this one 0.01 s step.
Endpoint position shift between the two arms, to check the braking box is not merely trading speed reduction for a large position penalty.
hypotheses: H1_unused_local_braking: the recorded applied input for update 32 leaves locally available braking authority unused, so the braking-box input yields a materially lower projected endpoint tip speed at this saved state.

H2_locally_bounded_braking: braking authority at this saved state is locally bounded (per-tendon force limits, geometry, or projected-model limits), so the braking-box input yields an endpoint tip speed close to the recorded input's.

H3_same_local_endpoint_from_different_mechanisms: if the two endpoints differ, objective weighting (terminal/holding tip-speed weights recorded as 0.0) and solver early-stop plan quality both predict the same local outcome and cannot be separated by this probe.

recommendations.rationale: Defer (do not execute or select in this phase) a single bounded prediction_braking probe at one saved late projected state where the tip moved fastest, comparing the recorded input with an instantaneous braking-box input over the fixed 0.01 s horizon. This locally measures whether the recorded commands left endpoint speed reduction unused, which bears on the command/authority mechanism versus the objective-weighting mechanism.

Defer a local_comparison check that adopts exactly one weight change (for example terminal tip-speed weighting) at a saved state whose effective horizon matches the authorized 0.01 s, since sampled late effective horizons of 1-5 intervals show matching is a real constraint. This is the only authorized operation that could locally separate objective weighting from solver early-stop effects, and it cannot establish closed-loop settling.

Defer any further progress on the solver-quality mechanism until the non-retained historical full warm plans / optimizer iteration traces are made available or a wider retained sample of updates is read; without them the early-stop and weighting hypotheses remain locally indistinguishable.

attribution.reason: Configuration gives zero weight to terminal and holding tip speed while position tracking carries weight 1.0, so the recorded plan objective is dominated by position; consistent with reach being achieved (error 0.0076 m) while terminal speed is still 0.6352 m/s. Raw weight magnitudes alone do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions.

Nearly every update was stopped by policy (relative_seed_improvement / budget_best_feasible) with only 1 Solve_Succeeded, mean update wall time 17.0752 s against a 0.01 s control period, and sampled late effective horizons collapsing to 1 interval; such plans are plausibly under-damped and give the receding-horizon controller little lookahead in which to null tip velocity.

Sampled late requested tensions reach 7.9904 N and 7.9439 N on single channels of an inventory limit of 8.0 N per tendon, so braking/redirect authority may be bounded; the degree of binding (and whether it mattered) was not quantified in this phase.

The scheduling contract for this run states synchronous controller calls complete before fixed-count backend steps and that wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time; the 35 deadline misses and the 17.0752 s mean update wall time are compute overruns, not simulated-time stalls, so they cannot by themselves displace the tip. They remain relevant only as a symptom of solver load.

Retained matched-interval velocity and projected-state offsets show the projected GVS prediction is close to but not identical to the full serial-backend endpoint; a saved-state probe over a single 0.01 s horizon cannot explain an entire settling failure, and no retained evidence ranks this against the command-objective and solver-quality mechanisms.

facts.statement: The run passed terminal reach (reach_passed true; terminal tip error 0.0076426 m inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance; tolerance 0.01 m) but failed sampled settling: late_max_speed_m_s 1.5810 and late_max_error_m 0.0581381 both exceed the settling criteria (position 0.01 m, speed 0.02 m/s, window 0.05 s), and terminal tip speed 0.6352 m/s remains above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit.

34 of 35 controller updates ended with solver status User_Requested_Stop versus 1 Solve_Succeeded; sampled stopping reasons are 'relative_seed_improvement' (updates 30, 31) and 'budget_best_feasible' (update 32); mean update wall time is 17.0752 s; sampled late effective horizons are 10 (update 2), 5 (30), 4 (31), 3 (32) and 1 (34) control intervals.
Controller configuration sets terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0 and holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0, with tracking_weight 1.0, velocity_weight 0.0001 and terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001.

Sampled requested tension commands reach 7.9904 N (update 30) and 7.9439 N (update 31) on individual channels; the retained evidence inventory lists a force limit of 8.0 N for each of the six tendons.

request_content.question: The run achieved terminal reach (reach_passed true; terminal_error_m ≈0.0076 m, inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance) yet failed its secondary settling objective: sampled_settling_passed false, with late_max_speed_m_s ≈1.58 m/s and late_max_error_m ≈0.0581 m both outside the settling criteria (0.01 m position / 0.02 m/s over a 0.05 s window), terminal_speed_m_s ≈0.635 m/s still far above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit, all 35 updates counted as deadline_misses (mean_update_s ≈17.08 s against control_period_s 0.01 s), and only 1 of 35 solver statuses reported Solve_Succeeded (34 User_Requested_Stop). Open question, with no root cause presumed in advance: what mechanisms plausibly explain the gap between successful terminal reach and failed secondary settling performance, and which candidate mechanisms can be distinguished using the retained evidence inventory together with the authorized bounded saved-state checks?
scope: Read-only inspection of the common inventory and summary already handed over, plus permitted reads of retained inventory entries via diagnosis.inspect_evidence / evidence.read: source.one_step_predictions, source.applied_tensions (/{update_id}/actual_tension_n), source.saved_projected_states (/{update_id}/measured_initial_state), source.plan_selection, source.solver_status, source.controller_horizon, source.force_limits (six tendons, each 8.0 N), and source.backend_motion sampled view (post-step times 0.01-0.35 s, 35 samples; raw gzip bytes not readable as JSON).

Explicitly authorized bounded saved-state numerical work under the host-supplied grant only: model.gvs@1.0.0, implicit_euler integration, integration_step_s 0.002, horizon_s 0.01, max_wall_s 300, configuration_scope saved_state_or_temporary_analysis, max_checks 1, operations limited to prediction_braking and local_comparison, within numerical limits local_solves <= 6 and prediction_evaluations <= 24.

Excluded from scope: production or configuration changes, controller-extension edits, closed-loop counterfactual replay, backend re-execution (backend_solves budget 0), and any claim of a dominant or causal settling cause; source.historical_full_plans (control_snapshots.json / full warm plans, optimizer iteration traces) is noted as not retained rather than assumed absent by failed reads.
stopping_conditions: Stop when retained evidence plus the authorized bounded checks have either bounded the plausible mechanisms consistent with failed settling despite successful reach, or demonstrated that the question is not answerable with the available inventory and tools.
Stop when the saved-state numerical budget is exhausted (local_solves 6, prediction_evaluations 24) or the 300 s wall limit for that work is reached.

Stop if differentiating candidate mechanisms would require the non-retained full warm plans / optimizer iteration traces or closed-loop counterfactual replay (stated capability gaps), rather than consuming further reads.
Stop after the request-phase evidence-turn allowance is spent and deliver the handoff with whatever the retained evidence supports.
